old.name: Marcel Petite — Fort Saint-Antoine affinage
old.label: CHEESE
old.hook: 100,000 Comté wheels aging in a 19th-c. military fort
old.text: 100,000 Comté wheels aging in a 19th-c. military fort Built 1879–1882 as part of the Séré de Rivières defensive system. In 1966, affineur Marcel Petite began renting it to age Comté in cold, slow, mountain conditions — 6–9 °C and 94–98 % humidity. Approximately 100,000 wheels age there at any time, on spruce shelves, for 10–20 months. Since 1966, over one million wheels have passed through the fort. Visits possible during summer; cheese available at the Maison du Comté and major fromageries (look for the dark-blue "Marcel Petite" label). Where Fort Saint-Antoine, near Pontarlier (1,100 m altitude) Address Fort Saint-Antoine, 25160 Saint-Antoine (near Pontarlier)

old.hook: 1 h · view over four glacial lakes from a single ridge
old.text: 1 h · view over four glacial lakes from a single ridge A short climb on the Frasnois plateau (35 km east of Lons) reaches the Belvédère des Quatre Lacs — a single ridge view down over Lac d'Ilay, Lac du Petit Maclu, Lac du Grand Maclu and Lac de Narlay, four glacial lakes left by the last ice age.
